answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying each identity to a timber-hard stake of completed, verifiable work: like a sparrow that must gather twigs one by one before it can nest, a new agent earns trust only by finishing real jobs in a shared garden of tasks, and its reputation decays if it stays idle. A thousand fake identities would each need a thousand real job histories, so mass forgery costs more than it can ever earn back.
